Hi Ammara — thanks for the heads up and the projection. We can support this, and there are a couple of ways to structure it depending on how you want to handle billing/commit: 

Option A — Temporary burst window (recommended for one-off campaigns):
- We can provision a temporary quota increase to 12M tokens/day for Mar 3–5.
- If usage exceeds the temporary quota, overages are billed at our on-demand overage rate.

Option B — Reserved burst pool with pre-paid buffer:
- Prepay for a burst allocation sized to your projection; unused tokens expire after the window.
- Overruns beyond the prepaid buffer billed at an overage rate (lower than on-demand).

For discounts: we can offer a one-time 15% discount on overage charges for customers who: (a) sign a short addendum and (b) commit to maintaining at least a 1x baseline monthly usage over the next 3 months. Alternatively, a smaller 10% ad-hoc discount is available without a commit.

Practical notes from our side:
- We need your exact peak token/minute estimate so Marissa (cc'd) can tune rate limits and caching.
- Billing: true-ups are handled monthly; your March usage would appear on the April invoice unless you request a pro-forma.

I've attached a provisional quote for the burst (pro_forma_burst_quote.pdf) — take a look and tell me which option you prefer. If you confirm by EOD Feb 27 we can lock the window and pre-wire capacity.

Would you like a 30-min sync tomorrow to walk procurement through options?

Subject: Re: Request: temporary rate limit increase & overage handling — implementation notes

Hi Ammara — quick technical notes to help size the burst and avoid unnecessary overage: 

- Token accounting: our billing counts consumed generation tokens (not user-side counts). If you have many short prompts with repeated prefixes, enabling prefix caching will reduce billable tokens.
- Rate limits: to minimize throttling risk, recommend a per-minute token burst cap (example: 1.5M tokens/min) rather than only a daily cap — this smooths traffic and reduces tail latency.
- Warm-up: very large spikes may take a short warm-up as caches populate; if you can pre-warm a small steady baseline in the 12–24 hours before Mar 3, it will reduce initial overage risk.
- Fallbacks: we can configure a soft-throttle + 429 responses vs hard-block. If you prefer failed requests to be queued, we can enable queuing but it may increase latency.

I've attached a short configuration note with recommended limits (burst_config_recommendation.md). Happy to run through the numbers if you share token/min peaks.

—Marissa
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachment: burst_config_recommendation.md (text - recommended rate-limit settings)
